title: ThreeTenBP complete hours across midnight
summary: Compare the complete-hours result on two dates against signed elapsed minutes. Qualify the adapter separately by constructing both endpoints independently on the JVM.

change.description: Account for incomplete days before counting whole time units.

notes: Both revisions agree with direct JVM calls through the hours adapter. The pinned parent returns 1 hour from 23:30 to 00:15 the next day and -1 in reverse. The fix returns zero in both directions. Same-day and sign-reversal checks pass on both.

Both the correct hours adapter and its wrong-unit control ran on both pinned artifacts. The hours adapter agreed with all 36,864 independently constructed calls in each revision. The MINUTES control differed on 36,672 pairs per revision. The first five strict attempts stopped at BigInteger.valueOf(long) in Duration.<clinit>. Their collected attempt bundles are discoverable from workflow_handoff.py.

Five linked retries on the original bindings now pass Duration initialization and stop at java.util.ServiceLoader.load in Chronology.<clinit> at line 148. The five tasks with fully symbolic initialization remain open. The public JVM review of ticks 94 and 97 refutes the parent clock claim, satisfies the fixed clock claim and rejects the same-day witness on domain membership. The two observed-initializer diagnostics and the intermediate local checker outputs are recorded in records/initialization-probes.json.

On JDK 21.0.13 the two observed Chronology registries were distinct empty ConcurrentHashMap objects. Separate native claims bind this state, the single-threaded String-key model and unwind 32. The checker refutes the parent clock, proves the fixed clock and proves reversal on each revision across all 36,864 pairs. It proves same-day preservation across all 18,432 admitted pairs. The three earlier 600-second timeouts and four receipt-schema refusals retain their own execution histories. The environment control in records/service-context.json changes only service discovery and reproduces a ServiceConfigurationError on both revisions.

The independent JVM driver identified all twelve sub-hour crossings in the quarter-hour grid. On this subset, the native checker established the fixed zero-hour result and refuted the parent with a JVM-replayed witness. The first batch job exited in argument parsing. Its superseding job published both receipts.
verdictLabel: 6,912 clock discrepancies before the fix on 36,864 ordered JVM calls
